Settled shape, all of it: threshold **`>=`** not `==` (a line already holding 4 must fail the check, or the `+` stays live exactly when it matters); scope is **per line item**, not per SKU (the SKU is already size + colour, so in normal shopping one line is one SKU); cap **consolidates to one line at 3** (free — `sum_quantities` already produces a single merged line item); callback order **merge → cap → 272's wishlist resume** (the wishlist move acts on a line the merge may have just consolidated and the cap just reduced; reversing it moves a quantity the shopper never saw); render guard is a secondary backstop that **no-ops while `useIsMutating()` is non-zero**, so it cannot race the callback; **keep the loop guard** — one correction in flight, one attempt per basket version, then stop and surface an error, because a write-on-render without it can rate-limit a shopper out of their own basket; **no action on the brief 4-then-3 flash** — observe real behaviour first.

**Pass criteria.**
1. Unit tests: line at 2 with max 3 → no change. Line at 3 → no change (`>=` boundary, the case `==` gets wrong is 4). Line at 4 → reduced to 3. Line at 5 → reduced to 3. Two lines of the same SKU at 2 each after a `sum_quantities` merge → one consolidated line at 3.
2. `useIsMutating()` non-zero → function returns without issuing a write. Asserted, not assumed.
3. Loop guard: two consecutive invocations against the **same** basket version issue exactly **one** write. A server rejection surfaces an error and does **not** retry indefinitely.
4. Callback order asserted: with all three armed, merge resolves before cap, and cap resolves before the wishlist resume. Assert on call order, not on final state — final state can look right with the wrong order.
5. Max value comes from `maxOrderQuantity.ts` (step 3.4), not a literal.
6. **State in the PR body that this is not end-to-end verifiable** until SFCC-268's `afterGET` hook is deployed (gate findings #1/#2 — the TSD is `v0.1 Draft`, Technical Lead sign-off Pending, and the live dev-sandbox probe found no `c_maxOrderQuantity` on any product, while Jira has 268 as Ready for SIT). The fallback path is what is being tested.

#### Step 4.3 — `useCartMessages`: one handler, one file to swap

**Changes.** Every message — success, error, warning — is emitted through **one** function, so SFCC-404 is later a renderer swap in a single file. A marker comment naming SFCC-404 sits at the emit site.

Interim surface is the base Chakra toast. **See open question 4 before writing the import line** — `overrides/app/hooks/use-toast.ts` does not exist, and creating it is a Tier 2 change this bundle has not budgeted for.

Copy (Figma leading, per the cards): single message uses the **product-named** variant, "Cloud 91 Small Clutch added to Wishlist"; already-in-wishlist is "An item in your bag already exists in Wishlist"; max-reached is "An item in your bag has reached maximum quantity". The generic stacked variant ("Item added to Wishlist") is only reachable once 404 lands with real stacking — a toast has no aggregation concept and is always on its own from the shopper's point of view, so the **interim toast uses the product-named copy**. Both divergences from SFCC-272's AC wording go on the deferred Jira comment; the cards are not edited.

**Pass criteria.**
1. `grep -rn "useToast\|toast(" overrides/app/pages/cart overrides/app/components/ui-kits/**/zimmCart*` shows exactly **one** emit site.
2. Each of the three copy strings is asserted verbatim in a test.
3. A Storybook `play` asserting a message queries `within(document.body)` with an inline comment citing `testing.md`'s portal exception — Chakra toasts portal outside `canvasElement` and this is the only sanctioned use of `within(document.body)`.
4. The SFCC-404 marker comment is present and names the ticket.

#### Step 4.4 — `ZimmCartItemActions` + pending-item-across-auth

**Changes.** Remove / Move to Wishlist as **underlined text links below the stepper** (SFCC-270 AC8, styled in B3's pass). Gap **24px**, not Figma's raw 25px — §11.10(4), snapped to the nearest tokenised value with a comment saying the design specified 25. Links `capitalize`, `textStyle="linkSm"`, `link/default` → `--zimm-color-text-default`.

Note the actions are **not** inside base `product-item` — it receives them as a `secondaryActions` prop from its caller. So this molecule is supplied by the container, and we do not fight the base structure to inject it.

Remove: item removed, drawer count decrements, totals update; quantity > 1 removes all units in one action.

Wishlist, guest: the existing `ZimmWishlistAuthDrawer` via `useWishlistAuthDrawer`, **one hook instance**, `intentId: 'cart-wishlist'`. Per gate #5, this is a **deliberate override** of two sources that say "login page" (SFCC-272 AC7 and Confluence CAI-018), justified by consistency with the four other auth-drawer surfaces — record it as an override, not as an AC reading. The `.docs/prd/cart.md` §2 paraphrase is the weaker justification and should not be the one cited.

Pending item held in **React state** (covers email-code and create-account, where the page never unloads) **and** session storage (covers the Apple/Google redirect). Read state first, fall back to storage, clear **both** together. Same **5-minute** age bound as the hook's own intent (`PENDING_WISHLIST_INTENT_MAX_AGE_MS`), so a stale item cannot be resumed.

Rejected and not to be revisited: one hook instance per line item (mounts a `useForm`, three `useAuthHelper`s, a `useAuthModal` and a drawer **per row** — a ten-item bag mounts ten of each, against a stated mobile-page-speed priority); adding an optional `itemId` to the shared `PendingWishlistIntent` (better long-term, but changes a shared hook with three existing call sites — raise separately).

#### Step 4.5 — `ZimmCartEmptyState`

**Changes.** A **discrete component, not inline JSX in the drawer**, so SFCC-277 is a swap in one file. 2. Removing the last item shows it (AC2), and the drawer header simultaneously reads `YOUR BAG IS EMPTY`.

4. Two-to-one column collapse asserted in the recipe test.

517	## 5.0 Verification standard (added 2026-09-19, applies to every remaining step, 3.6 onward)
518	
519	Six real, currently-shipped defects were found in commits already scored PASS on Design fidelity,
520	by a from-scratch re-audit that rendered the real components live instead of reading source and
521	Figma side by side. Every one of the six traces back to one of the gaps below. These are now
522	mandatory for every remaining step's Design-fidelity check — not optional rigor, a gate. When
523	dispatching Tester/Scorer for 3.6 onward, brief them with this section explicitly: they start
524	each run with no memory of today, so the standard has to be restated, not assumed carried over.
525	
526	1. **A rendered-output claim needs a live measurement citation, not a source read.** "The recipe
527	   sets `fontWeight: 500`" is not the same claim as "the rendered text measures `font-weight: 500`
528	   in a real browser" — the first can be true while the second is false. Every Design-fidelity
529	   PASS from here on cites an actual measured value (computed style, bounding box, or a real
530	   screenshot) against the actual Figma-sourced value, for every property being signed off, not
531	   just the ones that seem most at-risk.
532	2. **A wrapper's correct style does not prove a nested element inherits it.** Two of the six
533	   defects were exactly this shape: `textStyle`/`fontWeight` correctly set on a container, silently
534	   lost before reaching the actual visible text, because the nested element was either a Chakra
535	   component with its own competing theme registration (`Heading`, and by extension `Button`/
536	   `IconButton`/`Modal`/anything imported from `@chakra-ui/react` un-wrapped in a plain `chakra.*`
537	   factory) or a literal HTML tag with its own default rendering (`<b>`, via a base SFCC
538	   component). Whenever a style is applied above a boundary like that, verify the leaf text node's
539	   own computed style directly — inheritance is not something to assume across it.
540	3. **A previously-recorded "confirmed correct" is not permanent proof.** This exact document's own
541	   audit trail (`figma-reference/discrepancies.md`) both found real bugs *and*, twice, had to
542	   retract its own "confirmed" claims once they were checked against a real render instead of
543	   restated from a prior pass. Re-verify against a live render before citing an earlier pass as
544	   settled, especially for anything touching the same file again.
545	4. **Storybook `play` functions auto-run on load.** A live check against a story with a `play`
546	   function is measuring the *post-play* state by the time any normal wait resolves, not the
547	   initial seed — sample within ~100ms of mount if the true initial state matters, and never treat
548	   a play function's own scripted end-state as a seeding bug.
549	5. **Read the real, current JSX before asserting how two elements relate.** More than one
550	   mis-scoped finding this pass came from reasoning about layout from a written description
551	   instead of the actual current source — siblings vs. nested, same container vs. different, is
552	   checkable in seconds and shouldn't be inferred.
553	6. **A fix for one interaction can silently break a different one.** The focus-ring fix's first
554	   attempt passed its own new test and broke backdrop-click-to-close, undetected until the full
555	   existing suite was re-run. Any interaction/focus/event-handling change re-runs the component's
556	   *entire* existing test suite, not just the new assertion, before being called done.
557	7. **Mutation-test every new test, and disclose when jsdom genuinely can't.** Revert the fix,
558	   confirm the new test fails with the real wrong value; restore, confirm it passes. If a property
559	   (native `:focus-visible` matching is the known example so far) can't be made mutation-sensitive
560	   under jsdom, say so directly in the test's own comment rather than claim proof the test doesn't
561	   actually provide — the real proof in that case is the live-browser verification, cited as such.
562	8. **No AI attribution, no third-person references to any person, in any commit message.**
563	   Objective and technical only — what changed and why, not who caught it or confirmed it. Two
564	   rounds of whole-branch correction this pass were both this exact category.

## 5.0 Verification standard (added 2026-09-19, applies to every remaining step, 3.6 onward)

Six real, currently-shipped defects were found in commits already scored PASS on Design fidelity,
by a from-scratch re-audit that rendered the real components live instead of reading source and
Figma side by side. Every one of the six traces back to one of the gaps below. These are now
mandatory for every remaining step's Design-fidelity check — not optional rigor, a gate. When
dispatching Tester/Scorer for 3.6 onward, brief them with this section explicitly: they start
each run with no memory of today, so the standard has to be restated, not assumed carried over.

1. **A rendered-output claim needs a live measurement citation, not a source read.** "The recipe
   sets `fontWeight: 500`" is not the same claim as "the rendered text measures `font-weight: 500`
   in a real browser" — the first can be true while the second is false. Every Design-fidelity
   PASS from here on cites an actual measured value (computed style, bounding box, or a real
   screenshot) against the actual Figma-sourced value, for every property being signed off, not
   just the ones that seem most at-risk.
2. **A wrapper's correct style does not prove a nested element inherits it.** Two of the six
   defects were exactly this shape: `textStyle`/`fontWeight` correctly set on a container, silently
   lost before reaching the actual visible text, because the nested element was either a Chakra
   component with its own competing theme registration (`Heading`, and by extension `Button`/
   `IconButton`/`Modal`/anything imported from `@chakra-ui/react` un-wrapped in a plain `chakra.*`
   factory) or a literal HTML tag with its own default rendering (`<b>`, via a base SFCC
   component). Whenever a style is applied above a boundary like that, verify the leaf text node's
   own computed style directly — inheritance is not something to assume across it.
3. **A previously-recorded "confirmed correct" is not permanent proof.** This exact document's own
   audit trail (`figma-reference/discrepancies.md`) both found real bugs *and*, twice, had to
   retract its own "confirmed" claims once they were checked against a real render instead of
   restated from a prior pass. Re-verify against a live render before citing an earlier pass as
   settled, especially for anything touching the same file again.
4. **Storybook `play` functions auto-run on load.** A live check against a story with a `play`
   function is measuring the *post-play* state by the time any normal wait resolves, not the
   initial seed — sample within ~100ms of mount if the true initial state matters, and never treat
   a play function's own scripted end-state as a seeding bug.
5. **Read the real, current JSX before asserting how two elements relate.** More than one
   mis-scoped finding this pass came from reasoning about layout from a written description
   instead of the actual current source — siblings vs. nested, same container vs. different, is
   checkable in seconds and shouldn't be inferred.
6. **A fix for one interaction can silently break a different one.** The focus-ring fix's first
   attempt passed its own new test and broke backdrop-click-to-close, undetected until the full
   existing suite was re-run. Any interaction/focus/event-handling change re-runs the component's
   *entire* existing test suite, not just the new assertion, before being called done.
7. **Mutation-test every new test, and disclose when jsdom genuinely can't.** Revert the fix,
   confirm the new test fails with the real wrong value; restore, confirm it passes. If a property
   (native `:focus-visible` matching is the known example so far) can't be made mutation-sensitive
   under jsdom, say so directly in the test's own comment rather than claim proof the test doesn't
   actually provide — the real proof in that case is the live-browser verification, cited as such.
8. **No AI attribution, no third-person references to any person, in any commit message.**
   Objective and technical only — what changed and why, not who caught it or confirmed it. Two
   rounds of whole-branch correction this pass were both this exact category.

You are one of two forked verification angles for testing SFCC-11 plan.md Step 4.1 (`feat(auth): SFCC-250 passwordless basket merge`) on branch `feature/SFCC-11_cart`, repo `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa`. 1. `npx tsc --noEmit` — full output + exit code.
2. `npm run test -- --run` — the FULL suite. Report the exact final summary (files/tests passed/failed, verbatim).
3. 4. `node scripts/auditTokenUsage.mjs` — full output. The Implementer claims `overrides/app/hooks/**` is entirely outside this script's scanned paths — verify that claim by reading `scripts/auditTokenUsage.mjs`'s own path-matching logic, don't just trust it. Separately: `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/organisms/zimmWishlistAuthDrawer/index.stories.tsx` IS under `overrides/app/components/**` — but the audit script's own doc (`.claude/rules/overrideStyling.md`) says it excludes `*.stories.tsx` from scanning. Confirm whether it's excluded and whether the diff in that file (a Storybook decorator, not styling) is clean either way.

## Structural diff-scope checks

5. Diff the exported `UseWishlistAuthDrawerParams` and `UseWishlistAuthDrawerReturn` types in `overrides/app/hooks/useWishlistAuthDrawer.ts` between the current working tree and `git show HEAD:overrides/app/hooks/useWishlistAuthDrawer.ts` — confirm byte-for-byte identical (plan.md Step 4.1 pass criterion 5: "The hook's exported signature is unchanged"). Show your actual diff command and its output.
6. The hook has a SECOND `useEffect` (below the new merge-owning one), handling the social-IDP pending-intent resume via `readPendingWishlistIntent()`. Confirm it has ZERO diff against `git show HEAD:...` — extract just that effect's lines from both versions and diff them directly (plan.md pass criterion 3: "confirm the social-IDP effect itself has zero diff, not just that a new assertion was bolted onto its existing test").

## Regression-suite claim

7. The three real consumers of this hook are: `overrides/app/components/header/rightBar/index.tsx`, `overrides/app/components/drawer-menu/index.tsx`, `overrides/app/components/product-view/index.tsx` (confirmed via grep — these import/use `useWishlistAuthDrawer` or `ZimmWishlistAuthDrawer`). Find each one's own test file, plus `overrides/app/hooks/useWishlistAuthDrawer.test.tsx` itself, and run all four suites for real. Report exact pass/fail counts per file and combined — the Implementer claims "76/76 total across all four files."
8. Open each of the three CONSUMER test files (not the hook's own) and check: do they `vi.mock(...)` the `ZimmWishlistAuthDrawer` component (or the whole module containing it) wholesale, such that this hook's real body never actually executes inside those consumer tests? Quote the actual mock declaration lines as proof. The Implementer says this makes the regression pass "weak evidence — proves nothing about the mocked surface shape broke, not that merge behaves correctly on those live surfaces." Confirm or refute this independently with the actual mock code, don't just accept the framing.

## The undisclosed third file

9. `git status --porcelain` shows THREE modified files, but the Implementer's own report to the tester claimed only two (`useWishlistAuthDrawer.ts` and `.test.tsx`). The third is `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/organisms/zimmWishlistAuthDrawer/index.stories.tsx`. Its diff (already pulled) replaces a decorator that set `window.__STORE__` (a property nothing reads) with one that sets `window.__CONFIG__` — confirmed for real via `node_modules/@salesforce/pwa-kit-runtime/utils/ssr-config.client.js` line 21 (`return window.__CONFIG__`) and `.storybook/preview.tsx` lines 10-34 (global `__CONFIG__` shape is `{app: {login: {}, sites: [...]}}`, matching the new decorator's shape exactly) — that part is already independently verified, you don't need to re-verify the __CONFIG__-vs-__STORE__ mechanism itself. Your job:
   a. `git log --oneline -8 -- overrides/app/components/ui-kits/organisms/zimmWishlistAuthDrawer/index.stories.tsx` — is this file's history consistent with this being a fresh fix made alongside this step, or does it look like leftover uncommitted scope creep from something unrelated?
   b. Does this story have a `play` function, and is it referenced by any test anywhere (grep for the story name/`ZimmWishlistAuthDrawer` stories usage)? Determine if this fix is load-bearing for anything in Step 4.1's own pass criteria.
   c. Confirm independently that `useWishlistAuthDrawer.test.tsx` mocks `@salesforce/pwa-kit-runtime/utils/ssr-config` directly (look at the top of that file) — if true, this proves the Vitest suite for this step never touches the real `getConfig()`/`window.__CONFIG__` mechanism at all, meaning the stories.tsx fix cannot possibly be required infrastructure for this step's own two announced files to pass their tests. It's a genuinely separate, unrelated change bundled into the same uncommitted working tree.
   d. Give your own plain assessment: is the fix itself correct and complete (re-check the full new decorator body, not just the window-property-name part — e.g. does it still guard correctly, does removing the `typeof window !== 'undefined'` check matter given this is Storybook-only code that always runs in a browser context)? Is there anything wrong or incomplete about it?
   e. State plainly: this is a real, undisclosed file modification outside the step's announced two-file scope, regardless of whether the fix itself is good — the Implementer's own report to the tester said "only these two files," and that statement is false. This matters because `zm-implementer`'s mandate is to write only the files a step names and stop rather than expand scope, and AGENTS.md's "Minimal changes" rule requires proposing a larger change and waiting for confirmation, not silently bundling it in.

Report back everything with real evidence. Flag each finding CONFIRMED or PLAUSIBLE, and note whether it looks like a pattern that could recur elsewhere (UNIFORM) or is a one-off for this step (ONE-OFF).

header/index.tsx:252            onMyCartClick={onMyCartClick}

## Commit order

The step boundaries in §4 **are** the commit boundaries. That is what keeps a ~60-file PR
reviewable: eighteen scoped commits are navigable, three are not. Order matters more than it did
under §2 because there is no merge between stages.

| # | Commit | From §4 step |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `chore(ci): SFCC-11 add cart e2e area to qa.yml` | 0 |
| 2 | `feat(icons): SFCC-271 port PlusIcon to zimm.tsx` | §10 (1) |
| 3 | `fix(drawer): SFCC-315 correct ZimmDrawer xLarge width` | 1.1 |
| 4 | `chore(cart): SFCC-270 copy-first product-item + item-variant` | 2.1 — **STOP** |
| 5 | `feat(cart): SFCC-270 restyle override, fix item-name spread order` | 2.2 |
| 6 | `feat(cart): SFCC-315 ZimmCartDrawer organism` | 1.2 |
| 7 | `feat(cart): SFCC-271 ZimmQuantityStepper` | 3.1 |
| 8 | `feat(cart): SFCC-795 ZimmInlineMessage, error and warning states` | 3.2 |
| 9 | `feat(cart): SFCC-795 promotional price and discount label` | 3.3 |
| 10 | `feat(cart): SFCC-250 cartItemMapper and maxOrderQuantity util` | 3.4 |
| 11 | `feat(cart): SFCC-271-250 wire ZimmQuantityStepper and maxOrderQuantity into product-item` | 3.5 (inserted 2026-09-18) |
| 12 | `fix(a11y): SFCC-795 accessibility sweep` | 3.6 (renumbered from 3.5) |
| 13 | `feat(auth): SFCC-250 passwordless basket merge` | 4.1 |
| 14 | `feat(cart): SFCC-250 useCartMergeAndCap` | 4.2 |
| 15 | `feat(cart): SFCC-272 useCartMessages` | 4.3 |

| 17 | `feat(cart): SFCC-272 ZimmCartEmptyState` | 4.5 |
| 18 | `feat(cart): SFCC-275 ZimmCartButtonGroup and Pay marks` | 5.1 |
| 19 | `feat(cart): SFCC-315 wire the drawer trigger in _app and product-view` | §9 |

`commit-msg` enforces conventional format and `/generate-changelog` depends on it, so every message
is `type(scope): SFCC-NNN description`.

**Two things this ordering buys:**

- **Commit 18 puts the trigger last.** Under §2 it had to ship with B1. Here nothing is reachable
  until everything is built, and the review reads as "here is the thing, here is where we plug it
  in." A genuine gain from the single-PR shape.
- **Commit 4 preserves the copy-first pause intact.** Copy-first was never about branching — it is
  about not bundling the override copy with functional change. Commit 4 stops and waits for
  Marcel to observe all eight markers from the cart, the account wishlist page and a checkout
  summary. Nothing proceeds until that is recorded.

## 1. Create-account race trace — CONFIRMED not reachable on the nominal path

Read the current file directly. `onCreateAccount = () => { handleDrawerClose(); registerModal.onOpen(); }` (line 346). `handleDrawerClose` (line 232) calls `onClose()` from THIS hook's own `useDisclosure()` (line 125) — confirmed structurally separate from `registerModal`: `registerModal = useAuthModal(REGISTER_VIEW)` resolves to `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/hooks/use-auth-modal.js:402`'s `useAuthModal` export (NOT the `AuthModal` component at line 59 that owns `handleMergeBasket` — two different exports, confirmed via `grep -n "^export"`), and that hook's own source (lines 402-415) calls its own independent `useDisclosure()` internally and returns `{isOpen, onOpen, onClose, ...}` as plain props. `registerModal.onOpen()` therefore cannot touch this hook's own `isOpen`. Also confirmed via `grep -rn "registerModal" overrides/app/components/ui-kits/organisms/zimmWishlistAuthDrawer/index.tsx`: line 111 renders `<AuthModal {...registerModal} />` — the base SFCC `AuthModal` component, a real Chakra modal with its own overlay/focus-trap.

`isOtpAuthOpen` is only ever set `true` inside `onSendCode()` (line 289) after a successful passwordless send — nothing in the create-account path touches it.

Conclusion: on the direct sequence (guest opens wishlist drawer → clicks "Create an account" → completes registration in the SFCC register modal), `isOpen` and `isOtpAuthOpen` on this hook are both guaranteed false by the time `isRegistered` flips. **CONFIRMED**, and independently proven by mutation (c) below.

Edge case explored: `handleTriggerClick` (line 238) gates re-opening on `customer?.isRegistered` (from `useCurrentCustomer()`), a *different* source than the effect's own `isRegistered` (from `useCustomerType()`). If `customer.isRegistered` reads stale-false while `useCustomerType()`'s value is already true, a shopper could in theory re-click the wishlist trigger and set `isOpen = true` again while registration is completing. However this does **not** create a spurious merge: the effect's dependency array is `[isRegistered]` only, and `isRegistered` would already be `true` from a prior render in this scenario (not transitioning), so the effect does not re-fire merely because `isOpen` changed afterward. Separately, this path also requires clicking a trigger element behind a real, overlay-bearing Chakra modal (`<AuthModal {...registerModal} />`), which normally blocks pointer interaction with what's behind it. **PLAUSIBLE but not exploitable** — verified the dependency-array reasoning by source; did not verify the modal's overlay pointer-blocking live (that would need a real browser check, out of this angle's scope). Net: no reachable defect found here.

## 2. Mutation-hook object identity / dependency array — CONFIRMED no double-fire/staleness risk

The effect's deps are `[isRegistered]` only (line 212); `mergeBasket` (from `useShopperBasketsMutation('mergeBasket')`, line 144, a fresh-per-render mutation-hook result) is read inside the effect body but isn't a dependency. This is safe: React only re-invokes the effect when `isRegistered` itself changes (`Object.is` comparison) — `mergeBasket`'s identity churning across renders it *doesn't* re-run for is irrelevant, because the effect isn't watching it. Within the one execution that does fire, `mergeBasket.mutate(...)` runs synchronously against whatever `mergeBasket` closure was captured in that exact render — there's no async gap where a "later, stale" reference could get used instead, since `.mutate()` doesn't await and nothing is deferred. So: no double-merge, no stale-closure bug from this. Supporting indirect evidence: the identical `[isRegistered]`-only pattern already existed pre-diff for `onClose`/`setIsOtpAuthOpen`/`onAuthSuccess`, and the pre-existing "auto-close effect" test (`toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1)` on `onAuthSuccess`) has apparently never caught a double-fire under this same mechanism. **CONFIRMED** via React semantics, not just reasoned-about.

One pre-existing, out-of-scope-for-this-diff observation: `onAuthSuccess` (a caller-supplied prop, not guaranteed referentially stable) is also excluded from the deps array — a genuine stale-closure vector if a caller ever passes a non-memoized inline function, but this predates this diff (the array itself, `[isRegistered]`, is unchanged by the diff) and is not something this step introduced or worsened.

=== full commit metadata ===
commit dc8c7df3d7a46d6a78bad9d117a9156f32108780
Author: Marcel Angelo Navarro <marcel.a.n.navarro@accenture.com>
AuthorDate: Sat Sep 19 21:16:42 2026 +0800
Committer: Marcel Angelo Navarro <marcel.a.n.navarro@accenture.com>
CommitDate: Sat Sep 19 21:16:42 2026 +0800

fix(wishlist-auth-drawer): storybook story never rendered the real passwordless form

The story's decorator set window.__STORE__ to enable passwordless login
for the story, but getConfig() (@salesforce/pwa-kit-runtime) only ever
reads window.__CONFIG__ - a plain variable-name mismatch. The override
silently never applied, so isPasswordlessEnabled stayed false and the
story only ever rendered the "log in or create an account" gate screen,
never the actual email-entry form the component exists to show.

One consequence of the broken state: with no email input ever mounting,
initialFocusRef had nothing to focus, so Chakra fell back to focusing
the Close button - which looked identical to the close-icon-focus-ring
bug fixed elsewhere on this branch, but was actually just a symptom of
this unrelated Storybook-only config bug, not a real defect in the
component. Confirmed live: once the config is fixed, focus goes
straight to the email input with no detour through the close button.

Fix: set window.__CONFIG__ instead, matching the shape
.storybook/preview.tsx already establishes globally (login + sites),
overriding login/social on every render of this story rather than
guarding on "already set" - the story's own config requirement no
longer depends on decorator execution order relative to any other
story.

Verified: tsc clean, this component's own test suite unaffected (7/7
still passing - it doesn't depend on the story's decorator), lint
clean after one prettier auto-fix, live-confirmed via Playwright
against the running Storybook instance that the real form now renders
and focus lands correctly by default.

    fix(wishlist-auth-drawer): storybook story never rendered the real passwordless form
    
    The story's decorator set window.__STORE__ to enable passwordless login
    for the story, but getConfig() (@salesforce/pwa-kit-runtime) only ever
    reads window.__CONFIG__ - a plain variable-name mismatch. The override
    silently never applied, so isPasswordlessEnabled stayed false and the
    story only ever rendered the "log in or create an account" gate screen,
    never the actual email-entry form the component exists to show.
    
    One consequence of the broken state: with no email input ever mounting,
    initialFocusRef had nothing to focus, so Chakra fell back to focusing
    the Close button - which looked identical to the close-icon-focus-ring
    bug fixed elsewhere on this branch, but was actually just a symptom of
    this unrelated Storybook-only config bug, not a real defect in the
    component. Confirmed live: once the config is fixed, focus goes
    straight to the email input with no detour through the close button.
    
    Fix: set window.__CONFIG__ instead, matching the shape
    .storybook/preview.tsx already establishes globally (login + sites),
    overriding login/social on every render of this story rather than
    guarding on "already set" - the story's own config requirement no
    longer depends on decorator execution order relative to any other
    story.
    
    Verified: tsc clean, this component's own test suite unaffected (7/7
    still passing - it doesn't depend on the story's decorator), lint
    clean after one prettier auto-fix, live-confirmed via Playwright
    against the running Storybook instance that the real form now renders
    and focus lands correctly by default.
